name: Back Whisk
notes: Standard name (International Style waltz); the owner's class doesn't name it. Owner's description (2026-11-16): a variation on Box Turn (backward half) that ends with the legs crossed (the lead's left foot behind) and the shoulders open, not facing each other, ready for a promenade figure next. Steps 1 and 2 are the box turn's backward half exactly, including its quarter turn right on count 2, as the owner asked. On count 3 the lead's left toe goes just behind his right heel (owner's estimate), and both partners open an eighth (lead to his left, follow to her right) into a V: promenade position. The crossing foot ends about 0.25 behind and 0.05 across the standing foot, measured in the opened (final) facing, so the legs are crossed relative to the body; the offsets are rounded to the centimetre. Standard technique has little or no turn on count 2 of a back whisk; this follows the owner's version. Written with separate lead and follow rows on count 3 because the partners turn opposite ways; the offsets are from where each foot is before the step (lead's left at (-0.1, -0.5) facing east, follow's right at (-0.1, -0.1) facing west). expectEnd lists exact feet because promenade isn't a named stance yet.
